findings.title: SecurityAuditMiddleware never runs for the 401/403 cases it exists to log
findings.description: The middleware is placed after app.UseAuthorization() assuming the response status is finalized there, but ASP.NET Core's authorization middleware short-circuits (Challenge/Forbid) without calling next() on standard [Authorize] failures, which is virtually every endpoint. No IAuthorizationMiddlewareResultHandler is registered to preserve pipeline continuation, so the security-guide's "log auth denials" control is silently dead code for most real 401/403s.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement a custom IAuthorizationMiddlewareResultHandler (or hook the JWT OnForbidden/OnChallenge events) to log denials, rather than relying on downstream middleware the framework bypasses.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615.

findings.title: DiagnosticsController bypasses the service layer and repeats the outbound-call anti-pattern the style guide singles out
findings.description: Injects three DbContexts and IHttpClientFactory directly, runs raw SQL via SqlQueryRaw, hand-writes upsert/seed logic with manual SaveChangesAsync, and loops over collections making one outbound HTTP call per item inside local try/catch instead of the GlobalExceptionHandler.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract schema-introspection, sync, and geocoding concerns into dedicated services (mirroring the existing CustomerSyncService pattern) and let exceptions flow to GlobalExceptionHandler.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Partially addressed — the duplicated Nominatim geocoding is de-duplicated and moved onto the resilient named client. The wider service-layer extraction is outstanding; severity re-rated to medium (AdminOnly policy, schema endpoints are Dev/QA-only).

findings.title: Duplicated, ad hoc entitlement-catalog logic embedded in two controllers
findings.description: NotesController.GetMentionCatalog and EntitlementsController.GetCatalog both inject TradeUnitPreferencesDbContext directly and implement near-identical LINQ-heavy trade-unit/group expansion inline, each with its own try/catch(Exception) fail-open behavior.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract a shared IEntitlementsCatalogService consumed by both controllers; keep the documented fail-open behavior but implement it once.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Confirmed. Deliberately deferred: extracting IEntitlementsCatalogService touches NotesController, which several concurrently-active branches also touch, so it was the worst merge-conflict surface for the least value while fix_AuditPhase1Findings was in flight. Now unblocked.

findings.title: Trade-unit entitlement filtering is inconsistently applied across sibling bulk-read endpoints
findings.description: StoredGrainController and DpContractsController bind a raw string? tradeUnits and carry no [EnforceTradeUnitAccess] filter, unlike sibling Farms/Tickets/Contracts/Customers endpoints that bind List<string>? tradeUnits with enforcement. The shared attribute also silently no-ops on any future action parameter shape it doesn't recognize. Cross-check against permissions-model domain recommended.
findings.suggested_fix: Align both controllers to List<string>? tradeUnits + [EnforceTradeUnitAccess] (or add an explicit accepted-risk note), and log when no recognized parameter shape is found.
findings.notes: Cross-checked by the permissions-model audit: no live cross-trade-unit data bypass exists today (StoredGrainService/DpContractService independently apply entitlement scoping in the service layer as defense-in-depth, proven by DpContractServiceTests.cs). The controller-level binding/attribute inconsistency and the attribute's silent no-op on unrecognized shapes remain valid findings in their own right; see permissions.enforce-trade-unit-access-silent-noop and permissions.stored-grain-service-untested-entitlement-scoping. [2026-09-21] No live bypass — StoredGrainService and DpContractService each apply entitlement scoping independently (now pinned by StoredGrainServiceTests). The attribute's silent no-op half WAS fixed; the binding-shape inconsistency is left to align opportunistically when those controllers are next touched.

findings.title: GlobalExceptionHandler swallows all OperationCanceledException as an unlogged client-disconnect
findings.description: Maps OperationCanceledException to an unlogged HTTP 499 unconditionally without checking httpContext.RequestAborted.IsCancellationRequested, so an uncaught internal timeout would be silently discarded instead of logged at Error per error-handling.md.
findings.suggested_fix: Only treat as unlogged 499 when RequestAborted.IsCancellationRequested is true; otherwise log at Error as an infrastructure timeout.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615.

findings.title: Inconsistent EF Core command-timeout configuration across the four DbContexts
findings.description: OriginationDbContext and DpOdsDbContext set CommandTimeout(120); ApplicationDbContext and TradeUnitPreferencesDbContext fall back to the 30s SQL default even though the team already knows 30s is sometimes too tight.
findings.suggested_fix: Set an explicit CommandTimeout on ApplicationDbContext and TradeUnitPreferencesDbContext, or document why the 30s default is safe for both.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615.

findings.title: EF InMemory test-deviation tracking comment is stale and understates real usage
findings.description: The csproj's "DEVIATION" comment names only two files as users of the banned Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.InMemory package, but neither uses .UseInMemoryDatabase anymore while seven other untracked files do.
findings.suggested_fix: Update the csproj comment and migration plan to name the actual seven files so remediation is scoped against reality.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615.

findings.title: Controller test coverage gap - 9 of 23 controllers have zero test at any layer
findings.description: Only 8 controllers have a dedicated behavior test file; MeController stands out with untested role-resolution branching logic across three claim-name sources plus synthetic role injection.

findings.description: 15 of 21 repositories have zero direct test. TicketRepository (729 lines) and UsageRepository (915 lines) are the largest files in the folder with zero direct coverage of their query/mutation logic.

findings.description: Breaks the otherwise-consistent convention (34 files in Models/Responses) of one record-per-file with init-only properties.

findings.description: Bundles roughly 30 unrelated record types in a single file, versus the one-type-per-file convention followed elsewhere.

findings.title: Dead CancellationToken parameter in DiagnosticsController.StartElevatorGeocode
findings.description: Declares a CancellationToken parameter that is never used; the fire-and-forget Task.Run captures a fresh IServiceScopeFactory instead, making the parameter misleading dead code.

findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615.

findings.title: Duplicated hand-rolled parameter validation instead of a request DTO
findings.description: A private ValidateDashboardParams() checking tradeUnitKey/plantingYear is duplicated across 4 GET actions, while every other validated input in the codebase uses a request record with data annotations.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with a [FromQuery] request record using data-annotation validation.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Two scalar query-string params; binding a record to get annotations is more ceremony than the duplication costs. Recorded in STYLE-DEVIATIONS.md.

findings.title: CorrelationIdMiddleware accepts the inbound X-Correlation-Id header unbounded and unvalidated
findings.description: The header value is used verbatim (no length cap, no charset restriction), echoed into the response and threaded into every structured log entry, letting a caller inject an arbitrarily long or control-character value.
findings.suggested_fix: Cap length (e.g. 64 chars) and restrict to alnum+hyphen, falling back to a generated GUID otherwise.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615.

findings.title: Repository interface return-type inconsistency
findings.description: Most repository interfaces return Task<List<T>> for read-only collections while a minority correctly return Task<IReadOnlyList<T>> per the style guide.
findings.suggested_fix: Standardize on IReadOnlyList<T>/IReadOnlyCollection<T> for read-only collection return types.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Worth doing as one sweep, not opportunistically — a half-converted set is worse than a consistent one. Recorded in STYLE-DEVIATIONS.md.

findings.title: Redundant re-fetch in ProducerDetailsRepository.UpsertAsync
findings.description: After rebuilding grain-on-farm and contact child rows in memory and saving, the method re-queries them via separate calls instead of reusing the in-memory values.
findings.suggested_fix: Project the response directly from the in-memory grainItems/contactItems collections instead of re-querying after save.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] REJECTED as incorrect. The two post-save reads are NOT redundant: a null contacts list means "not provided" and deliberately PRESERVES existing rows, so on that path the request carries nothing and the DB is the only source; and GetContactsAsync returns primary-first, which the normalized request list does not guarantee, so the response order would change by path. Applying the suggested fix would ship a bug. Reason documented in ProducerDetailsRepository.UpsertAsync.

findings.title: Business-critical "god" components carry zero test coverage
findings.description: Five files containing the app's most complex logic (bid pricing/map rendering, contract/print orchestration, race-guarded multi-fetch data loading, BFS producer-linking, saved-list/NLQ enrichment) are entirely inside components, up to 4180 lines, with no matching .spec.ts.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract data-fetching/business logic into dedicated services (more unit-testable), then add specs starting with the highest-risk flows.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Confirmed; duplicate of test-gaps.angular-god-components.

findings.title: Route guards can hang navigation indefinitely instead of failing closed
findings.description: When MSAL interaction settles with no active account, the guard's source pipe returns EMPTY, so the backing ReplaySubject never emits and ready$() never completes -- navigation silently stalls with no redirect and no error.
findings.suggested_fix: Race ready$() against a timeout or an "unauthenticated" signal that resolves to router.createUrlTree(['/']) so the guard always settles.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615.

findings.title: @it/design-system (scoular-*) classes are effectively unused across the shared UI kit
findings.description: Every shared primitive hand-rolls Tailwind variant maps instead of emitting scoular-btn/scoular-badge/scoular-card/scoular-modal/scoular-table; warning/destructive variants also use generic Tailwind colors instead of mandated scoular-yellow/scoular-red tokens. Drift is app-wide since most feature templates build on these wrappers.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the shared primitives to map variant/size inputs onto scoular-* classes so feature templates inherit the fix without individual changes.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] This app standardised on the Tailwind brand colour tokens rather than scoular-* component classes. Recorded in STYLE-DEVIATIONS.md.

findings.title: Components own state that AppStateService should own, and already reach into it directly
findings.description: AppStateService exposes ~30 pieces of state as raw writable signal() fields (not .asReadonly()). Components call this.appState.queryLibrary.set(...) directly, bypassing any service-level update method, so multiple unrelated components can independently mutate shared app state.
findings.suggested_fix: Expose state via .asReadonly() and require all writes to go through explicit service methods.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Confirmed but over-rated: 38 raw signals with no asReadonly() is accurate, but "components already reach into it directly" is 2 call sites across all features, not a pattern.

findings.title: No typed error contract; silent error swallowing across services and components
findings.description: No typed error class exists anywhere in the app. DataPreloadService collapses every dataset failure to [] with no signal to the UI; roughly two dozen .subscribe({ error: () => {} }) blocks swallow failures with no toast, no error state, and no distinguishable empty-vs-failed outcome.
findings.suggested_fix: Introduce one ApiError-style type built centrally in ApiService's error handling, and route every swallowed error: callback through toastService.error(...) or a component errorMessage signal.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Confirmed and outstanding — a design item. Undercounted, in fact: 34 `error: () => {}` sites plus 13 catchError(() => of([])) in the preload service. The traceId half was fixed (handleError now carries it) and 401 now surfaces a session-expired toast.

findings.title: any type used in ~20+ locations against the explicit no-any rule
findings.description: any is concentrated in Leaflet map interop (_map: any, (marker as any).customerId, (L as any).markerClusterGroup) and in dynamically-shaped HTTP/forkJoin results.
findings.suggested_fix: Type Leaflet interop using the already-installed @types/leaflet/@types/leaflet.markercluster, and give forkJoin call sites a proper Partial<Record<...>> result interface.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Confirmed — 39 non-spec sites, concentrated in Leaflet interop. Outstanding.

findings.title: Dead duplicate CustomerMapComponent with a colliding selector
findings.description: A second, different implementation of CustomerMapComponent shares the app-customer-map selector with the live one; the duplicate is imported nowhere in the app.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the orphaned components/customer-map/ folder, or confirm intent and rename/consolidate to avoid a same-selector collision if both are ever imported together.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615.

findings.title: Inconsistent OnPush adoption on fully signal-driven components
findings.description: Only 20 of 49 components set ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush; most of the shared UI kit and several feature components are entirely input()/signal-driven yet omit it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush to the remaining signal-driven components (low-risk, mechanical change).
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Confirmed and deliberately deferred: 29 components, and OnPush breaks silently wherever a parent mutates an array in place. The actual per-cycle cost the perf findings described was removed by converting the hot getter to a computed().

findings.title: Function calls used directly in template bindings instead of computed()/pipes
findings.description: Recurring pattern (getContacts(), getPricingLinesForContract(contract), commodityChipClass(), ticketDisplayNumber()) re-sorts/re-filters/re-formats on every change-detection pass rather than being memoized.
findings.suggested_fix: Convert the highest-traffic offenders (especially ones that sort/filter arrays) to computed() signals or pure pipes.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Confirmed; part of the deferred OnPush/memoisation work.

findings.title: Broad unit-test coverage gap beyond the god components
findings.description: 31 of 49 components (63%) have no .spec.ts, including the entire shared UI kit and load-bearing utils like the BFS-based linked-producers.ts.
findings.suggested_fix: Prioritize specs for shared primitives (high reuse, low cost to test) and untested utils with real branching logic.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Partially addressed — linked-producers.ts (the BFS utility, including all three non-termination cases) is now covered. The shared UI-kit component specs remain outstanding.

findings.title: Production bootstrap failures are silently swallowed
findings.description: bootstrapApplication(...).catch only logs in non-production. A production bootstrap failure produces a blank page with zero diagnostic trail.
findings.suggested_fix: Log unconditionally (or route through the telemetry sink used elsewhere) and render a minimal static fallback message on bootstrap failure.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Confirmed; duplicate of logging.bootstrap-failure-not-logged.

findings.title: Stale security comment about bypassSecurityTrustHtml usage
findings.description: main.ts's threat-model comment states no bypassSecurityTrustHtml usage anywhere in the app, but highlight.pipe.ts does call it (safely, on pre-escaped input, but with no test coverage guarding that).
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the main.ts comment to note the one intentional, escaped exception, and add a spec for highlight.pipe.ts asserting it rejects unescaped HTML.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615.

findings.title: Duplicated crop/commodity taxonomy logic across multiple utils
findings.description: Several utils independently build overlapping commodity-code lookup/conversion maps rather than sharing one source; the codebase's own comments reference a past bug caused by exactly this kind of duplication.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract one shared builder/lookup table that the individual utils consume.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Confirmed; duplicate of clean-slop.duplicated-commodity-taxonomy. Same reasoning.

findings.title: Three mutually-inconsistent definitions of the same tables (ProducerDetails, SavedLists) across ad hoc scripts, qa-setup, and EF migrations
findings.description: CreateProducerDetailsTable.sql, qa-setup.sql, and the real EF snapshot all disagree on column types and presence; whichever script actually ran in a given environment silently determines that environment's real schema, independent of and diverging from the EF model.
findings.suggested_fix: Archive/delete the stale Scripts/*.sql table-creation files; treat EF migrations as the single source of truth, and reconcile any environment seeded from the wrong script.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615.

findings.title: Hand-rolled DDL plus faked EF migration history for BidSheet tables
findings.description: These scripts hand-build the BidSheetLocations/BidSheetLocationBids schema in raw SQL, then insert a row into __EFMigrationsHistory claiming a migration already ran. EF can never detect drift between this hand-written DDL and its own model.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace this pattern with a real EF migration; add a verification step that diffs the live schema against the EF snapshot before backfilling history rows.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615.

findings.title: Migration Down() applies destructive, unrelated schema changes that Up() never made
findings.description: Up() only adds a nullable Notes.CustomerCode column, but Down() also runs two unrelated AlterColumn calls widening ProducerDetails.Id and Notes.Id from int to bigint. Rolling back would silently widen both PK columns.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the two stray AlterColumn calls from Down() so it only reverses the CustomerCode addition.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Real, but accepted: migrations run forward only (deploy workflows only ever run `database update`), and rewriting an applied migration's Down() is riskier than leaving it. Recorded in STYLE-DEVIATIONS.md.

findings.title: LinkedProducerIds column type mismatch between script and canonical schema
findings.description: AddLinkedProducerIds_ProducerDetails.sql adds the column as VARCHAR(1000), while qa-setup.sql's canonical definition uses NVARCHAR(1000). If the VARCHAR version is live anywhere, non-ASCII producer names/IDs would be silently corrupted.
findings.suggested_fix: Standardize on NVARCHAR(1000) in both places and reconcile via a single tracked migration.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615.

findings.title: PopulateMbpLocationSynonym.sql runs an unguarded mass-delete MERGE
findings.description: The MERGE ... WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN DELETE has no row-count threshold check before committing -- a bad/truncated source export would silently mass-delete location master rows with only a PRINT statement as a trace.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a pre-commit guard that aborts/rolls back if the delete count exceeds a sane percentage of current rows.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615.

findings.title: Ambiguous DisplayName join can mis-assign UPN during CreatedBy backfill
findings.description: The remediation script joins Notes.CreatedBy to UserTradeUnitSnapshot.DisplayName to resolve a UPN, but DisplayName is not unique in that table, so rows with duplicate DisplayNames can get an arbitrary/wrong UserId.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip or flag rows where COUNT(DISTINCT UserId) > 1 for a given DisplayName instead of joining blindly.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Confirmed. Blocked on a fact nobody recorded: has B4_migrate_createdby.sql run in each environment? If PROD is still pending, the non-unique DisplayName join must be fixed first; if it has run, the script should be archived.

findings.title: Orphaned/stale ops script targets a column that no longer exists
findings.description: The script drops ProducerPlantingIntentions.EstimatedYield, but that column is absent from the current expected schema, indicating stale scripts aren't being cleaned up after use.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the script from the repo now that its one-time purpose is complete, or move completed ops scripts to an archive folder.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615.

findings.title: GroupTradeUnits.GroupId foreign key has no supporting index
findings.description: GroupTradeUnits.GroupId has an explicit FK to TradeUnitGroups but only TradeUnitCode is indexed on that table; ON DELETE/ON UPDATE behavior is also left unspecified.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a nonclustered index on GroupTradeUnits.GroupId and specify explicit delete/update behavior on the FK.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Not applicable: migration 20260513051734_RemoveTradeUnitCatalog drops GroupTradeUnits. The only creator was scripts/qa-setup.sql, a stale pre-CI bootstrap script now deleted.

findings.title: CustomerTradeUnit->Customer cascade delete breaks the codebase's own documented pattern
findings.description: Every other FK to Customer in this file is explicitly NoAction with a comment explaining it's deliberate. CustomerTradeUnit's Customer FK is Cascade with no comment, so a Customer rebuild could silently delete manually-curated rows.
findings.suggested_fix: Change CustomerTradeUnit's Customer FK to NoAction/Restrict to match the established pattern, or add a comment justifying the difference.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Confirmed and TIME-SENSITIVE. Inert today (all rows come from the ODS sync) but feature_NewCustomerTradeUnits introduces manually curated rows, after which a Customer rebuild silently destroys hand-entered membership. Decide before that feature starts.

findings.title: Unjustified string-typed primary keys
findings.description: ElevatorCache uses ElevatorCode (nvarchar(50)) as its PK, and UserTradeUnitSnapshot uses a composite key of two string columns, with no documented justification per the style guide's surrogate-key requirement.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a comment documenting why the external code is used as a natural key, or introduce a surrogate INT/BIGINT identity PK with the code as a unique index instead.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] ElevatorCode is the natural key from ODS and every lookup is by code; the snapshot composite IS the row identity. Recorded in STYLE-DEVIATIONS.md.

findings.title: FromSqlRaw fed a C#-interpolated string instead of FromSqlInterpolated
findings.description: SearchAsync/SearchOdsAsync build the WHERE clause via C# string interpolation before passing to FromSqlRaw/SqlQueryRaw with separate SqlParameters; values are parameterized correctly today, but the pattern is one accidental edit away from real injection.
findings.suggested_fix: Build the WHERE clause via StringBuilder/string.Concat (not $"...") so the pattern can't be miscopied later with genuinely interpolated data.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Confirmed — values are correctly parameterised today, so no live injection path; converting to FromSqlInterpolated is still worth doing.

findings.title: Foreign keys added WITH NOCHECK are never revalidated
findings.description: Three FKs were added WITH NOCHECK to skip validating pre-existing orphan rows, with a comment noting they should be revalidated later via WITH CHECK CHECK CONSTRAINT -- no later migration ever does this.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a follow-up migration that cleans up orphan rows and runs WITH CHECK CHECK CONSTRAINT on all three, or explicitly document this as an accepted permanent gap.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Confirmed — three FKs added WITH NOCHECK and never revalidated; the only occurrence of WITH CHECK CHECK CONSTRAINT in the repo is the comment saying to do it. Next step is a read-only orphan count per environment, not a code change.

findings.title: Non-idempotent ALTER scripts will fail if re-run
findings.description: These scripts run bare ALTER TABLE ADD statements with no IF NOT EXISTS guard, so re-running any of them against an environment where they already applied will error out.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap each ALTER in an IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT * FROM sys.columns ...) guard per the migration standards template.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615.

findings.title: Location master data hardcoded independently in two scripts
findings.description: Both scripts embed roughly a thousand-plus literal location rows independently rather than one sourcing from the other's target table, guaranteeing drift over time.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the coverage-check script query the populated table directly instead of maintaining a separate hardcoded list.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Half addressed: CheckMbpLocationCoverage.sql was deleted as a spent one-off. PopulateMbpLocationSynonym.sql stays (it is the live QA/PROD load path) and gained a row-count guard on its MERGE.

findings.title: Y/N flags modeled as NVARCHAR(1) instead of BIT on app-owned tables
findings.description: OurFacility, PushNotificationsHidden, and CashBidsHidden are documented as Y/N values but typed as string/nvarchar(1) rather than bool/BIT, pushing string-comparison logic into every consumer.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a bool property with HasConversion to Y/N (or migrate the columns to BIT) for these two app-owned tables.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] MbpLocationSynonym is a faithful mirror of TSCPRDLIB.MBPLOCSYN and is reloaded from that export; Y/N is the source system's shape, so converting breaks the mirror. Recorded in docs/application-context/STYLE-DEVIATIONS.md.

findings.title: ExecuteSqlRawAsync built via string interpolation of a compile-time constant
findings.description: Uses C# interpolation to splice in a private constant into the SQL text; the real runtime cutoff value is passed safely via the parameterized overload, so there is no real injection risk, but it matches the letter of the no-string-interpolated-SQL rule.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the interpolated string with plain string concatenation for lint/style compliance.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] The interpolated value is a private const; the runtime value goes through the parameterised overload. No injection path. Recorded in STYLE-DEVIATIONS.md.

findings.title: SELECT c.* used in raw SQL instead of an explicit column list
findings.description: FromSqlInterpolated calls use SELECT c.* mapped onto full entity types, brittle to schema drift; TicketRepository.cs already documents why the team prefers naming every column explicitly elsewhere in the same codebase.
findings.suggested_fix: Enumerate the mapped columns explicitly, matching TicketRepository's existing pattern.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] FromSqlInterpolated mapping onto a full entity, where the entity is the shape contract. Revisit per-query if an ODS view change breaks one. Recorded in STYLE-DEVIATIONS.md.

findings.title: N+1 query in bid-insert race-reconciliation retry path
findings.description: ReconcileDuplicateBidInsertsAsync issues one FirstOrDefaultAsync DB round trip per colliding bid inside a foreach loop instead of a single batched lookup; low impact since it only runs on the rare unique-constraint-violation retry path.
findings.suggested_fix: Batch-load all potentially colliding rows in one query keyed by the tuple set, then reconcile in memory (mirroring BulkUpsertBidsAsync).

findings.title: Unvalidated inbound X-Correlation-Id is trusted as the structured-log TraceId for every log line
findings.description: CorrelationIdMiddleware takes the inbound header with no length cap, character filter, or format check, then RequestContextMiddleware puts it into an ILogger.BeginScope TraceId field that every logger in the request inherits, plus it's echoed into log message templates in SecurityAuditMiddleware, GlobalExceptionHandler, and the OnAuthenticationFailed handler in Program.cs, and forwarded outbound via CorrelationIdOutboundHandler. An attacker-supplied value becomes the primary correlation key across the whole telemetry pipeline, enabling log-forging/injection into KQL-queried fields, correlation-dashboard pollution, cross-request correlation spoofing, and unbounded-length values inflating Log Analytics ingestion cost.
findings.suggested_fix: In CorrelationIdMiddleware, accept the inbound header only if it matches a safe format (e.g. GUID or bounded alphanumeric/hyphen, <=64 chars); otherwise discard it and mint a fresh ID, same as the no-header path.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Re-verified: CorrelationIdMiddleware.IsWellFormed() now rejects anything over 64 chars or outside [A-Za-z0-9-_.:], falling back to Activity.TraceId or a fresh GUID. Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615. Still resolved.

findings.title: Angular client has no error/telemetry logging service at all, contradicting the team's own mandatory pattern
findings.description: developer-docs/CLAUDE.md states client-side Application Insights is required for any Scoular Angular SPA using MSAL, and prescribes a full pattern (AppInsightsService, AppInsightsErrorHandler, MSAL event forwarding, CSP allow-list, per-environment connection string). None of it exists: the App Insights web/angular packages are absent from client/package.json, no app-insights.service.ts exists, and ErrorHandler is bound to GlobalErrorHandler which only console.errors in dev mode and shows a generic toast, reporting nothing in production. MSAL events are consumed only to drive an isAuthenticated signal and are never forwarded to telemetry. Every unhandled Angular exception, MSAL auth/token failure, and route or bootstrap failure in production is completely invisible to the team.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement the AppInsightsService/AppInsightsErrorHandler/MSAL-telemetry-forwarder pattern already specified in developer-docs/CLAUDE.md, wire it into main.ts's providers, and add the connection string plus CSP allow-list entries per environment.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Re-verified: client/package.json still has no @microsoft/applicationinsights-* dependency, no app-insights.service.ts exists anywhere under client/src, and ErrorHandler is still bound to GlobalErrorHandler (console-only in dev, silent in prod). Still the audit's only open critical; unchanged since 2026-09-19. Needs the same decision as before: implement client App Insights, or amend developer-docs/CLAUDE.md to stop mandating it.

findings.suggested_fix: Always log the bootstrap error (drop the non-production guard, or at minimum always console.error) and, once client-side telemetry exists, call trackException there unconditionally since DI-provided services aren't available yet.

findings.title: Backend error traceId is never read or shown by the Angular client, breaking the support-reference workflow
findings.description: GlobalExceptionHandler builds a user-facing 500 message including a (Ref: {traceId}) specifically so a user can hand that reference to support, and every ApiErrorResponse.Error.TraceId is populated on every error response. ApiService.handleError parses the error message/details but never reads .traceId, so it never reaches the console, a toast, or any telemetry call, silently dropping the correlation ID on every frontend error path.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract error.error.error.traceId in ApiService.handleError, attach it to the thrown Error object, and surface it in the toast/telemetry call so a user-reported failure can be traced back to server logs.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Re-verified: ApiService.handleError (api.service.ts:117-118) now reads errObj.traceId and attaches it to the thrown Error. Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615. Still resolved.

findings.title: Scheduled background services don't mint a per-run correlation id
findings.description: CustomerSyncBackgroundService, UsageAggregationBackgroundService, and UsageTrackingBackgroundService log via ILogger with good level discipline but never attach a per-execution id/scope, unlike HTTP requests which get TraceId via RequestContextMiddleware. If a nightly sync run misbehaves, there's no single field to filter Log Analytics down to just that run's log lines.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap each ExecuteAsync run body in an ILogger.BeginScope(new { RunId = Guid.NewGuid() }) so all lines from one execution are filterable together.
findings.notes:
[2026-09-21] Re-verified and status corrected from resolved to open: CustomerSyncBackgroundService and UsageAggregationBackgroundService now wrap each run in _logger.BeginScope(...RunId...) (fixed via PR #615), but UsageTrackingBackgroundService — one of the three files this finding names — still has no per-run scope; its ExecuteAsync logs (start/stop/batch errors) carry no RunId. The fix was only 2/3 applied.
[2026-09-21] Re-run reopened this as 2/3 applied. Verified: the third service was skipped on purpose (PR #615) with the reasoning recorded in code. Recorded as accepted rather than open.
findings.accepted_rationale: Per-run scope is applied to the two scheduled jobs (CustomerSyncBackgroundService, UsageAggregationBackgroundService). UsageTrackingBackgroundService is deliberately excluded and says so in a comment at the top of ExecuteAsync: it is a continuous 5-second flush loop (~17k iterations/day) that logs nothing but errors, so a per-flush id would add Log Analytics cardinality without answering a question anyone asks; its error lines already carry batch context.

findings.title: User's UPN (email-shaped identifier) is written into every structured log line app-wide

The style guide prefers stable non-sensitive identifiers over emails when a user identifier is needed; this is plausibly an intentional accountability tradeoff for an internal B2B app, but it isn't documented as a deliberate data-classification decision.
findings.suggested_fix: Either confirm and document this as an accepted tradeoff, or switch the logged identifier to the Azure AD object id with UPN resolved only at query time by a support tool with appropriate access.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Re-verified: RequestContextMiddleware still resolves preferred_username (UPN) into the UserId scope field on every request. Formally accepted and recorded as AR-09 in SECURITY-REVIEWS/ACCEPTED-RISKS.md (Low, CWE-532, accepted 2026-09-21, review 2027-09-21). Unchanged, still accepted.

findings.title: Per-row template binding invokes an O(tickets x contracts) getter on every change-detection pass
findings.description: tickets-table.component.html calls spotTicketIds.has(ticket.id) inside a @for over group.tickets. spotTicketIds is a plain TS getter, not a computed(), that rebuilds a Set by iterating every ticket and, for each unapplied one, running contracts.some(...) over the full contracts array. Because it's called once per rendered ticket row and the component has no ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush, this recomputes on every CD cycle triggered anywhere in the app, multiplying rendered-row-count x ticket-count x contract-count work repeatedly. For a producer with hundreds of tickets and dozens of contracts, this is a real, likely user-visible jank source on the Tickets tab.
findings.suggested_fix: Convert spotTicketIds (and the sibling unappliedTickets getter) to computed() signals, and add changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush to the component.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615. [2026-09-21 re-verified] Confirmed in code: tickets-table.component.ts:132 now declares `spotTicketIds = computed<Set<number>>(...)` with an inline comment naming this exact finding, so it recomputes only when tickets()/contracts() signals change rather than on every CD pass. OnPush itself is still not applied to this component, but that gap is separately tracked under performance.angular-onpush-coverage-gap, and the quadratic-recompute defect this finding targeted is genuinely closed via memoization regardless of change-detection strategy.

findings.title: Primary contracts table has no OnPush and repeats uncached per-row lookups in template bindings
findings.description: contracts-table.component.ts declares no changeDetection (defaults to Default strategy), so it re-runs full change detection on every app-wide tick. Its template calls getAppliedTickets(contract) (a .filter() over the full tickets() input with no memoization) and getPricingInfo(contract) up to 3 times per row, plus getPricingLinesForContract(contract) 4-5 times per expanded row. This is the table rendered on every customer-profile Contracts tab view, one of the most frequently opened screens.
findings.suggested_fix: Add ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush; memoize getAppliedTickets/getPricingInfo results per contract (e.g. a computed() Map similar to the existing pricingLinesMap/_deliveryStatsCache pattern already used for getDeliveryStats).
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Confirmed; part of the deferred OnPush work.

findings.title: Function calls used directly in template bindings re-run expensive work on every change-detection pass
findings.description: Verified across customer-profile.component.html (getContacts() inside a @for, backed by a fresh array allocation + sort on every evaluation), contracts-table.component.html (getPricingLinesForContract(contract) called 4 times per expanded row, ticketDisplayNumber(ticket) per applied-ticket row), and dashboard.component.html (commodityChipClass(chip.colorKey) inside a @for over planting chips). None of these are memoized via computed()/pipes.
findings.suggested_fix: Convert the highest-traffic offenders (especially ones that sort/filter arrays) to computed() signals or pure pipes.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Confirmed; duplicate of angular.function-calls-in-template-bindings.

findings.title: Roughly half of standalone components skip OnPush change detection, compounding into full-tree re-evaluation
findings.description: Of 47 component.ts files, only 20 declare ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush; the rest (including activity-summary, producer-insights, edit-customer-dialog, planting-intentions-table, home.component.ts, and both customer-map variants) run Default strategy. activity-summary.component.ts and tickets-table.component.ts in particular do multiple filter/reduce/sort passes over customer/contract/ticket arrays in plain getters/methods rather than computed(). This is a systemic risk that compounds any signal update in AppStateService into full-tree re-evaluation.
findings.suggested_fix: Adopt OnPush as the default for new/touched components; prioritize converting the customer-profile subtree (home -> contracts-table, tickets-table, activity-summary) since that's the highest-traffic screen.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Confirmed; duplicate of angular.inconsistent-onpush-adoption.

findings.title: N+1 query in bid-insert race-reconciliation retry path is broader than initially scoped
findings.description: BidSheetRepository.ReconcileDuplicateBidInsertsAsync loops over EVERY ChangeTracker entry in EntityState.Added for BidSheetLocationBid, not just the one that triggered the unique-constraint exception, issuing one FirstOrDefaultAsync per entity to check for a DB-side collision. Triggered from BulkUpsertBidsAsync's SaveChanges catch block, so a single unique-constraint race during a large bulk upsert (many locations x commodities x months) fans out to one round trip per pending insert, not just per actual collision.
findings.suggested_fix: Batch-load all potentially colliding rows in one query keyed by the tuple set, then reconcile in memory (mirroring BulkUpsertBidsAsync).
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615. [2026-09-21 re-verified] Confirmed in code: BidSheetRepository.cs:463-503 ReconcileDuplicateBidInsertsAsync now issues one batched query keyed by distinct LocationId/CropYear across all pending Added entities, then reconciles in-memory via a dictionary keyed on (LocationId, CommodityCode.ToUpperInvariant(), CropYear, Month) -- replacing the prior per-entity FirstOrDefaultAsync fan-out. Inline comments explicitly reference the N+1 pattern being avoided.

findings.title: [ApiController] automatic model-validation responses never use the standard error envelope
findings.description: All 23 controllers carry [ApiController], and Program.cs never configures ApiBehaviorOptions.InvalidModelStateResponseFactory. So any data-annotation failure on the 21 validated request DTOs is short-circuited by the ASP.NET Core framework default into RFC7807 ValidationProblemDetails JSON before GlobalExceptionHandler or the app's own ValidationException ever run. This is the single most common validation-failure path across the whole write surface, and it never matches the mandated {error:{code,message,details,traceId,timestamp,instance}} shape, while the exact same conceptual failure thrown manually as ValidationException elsewhere produces a completely different shape.
findings.suggested_fix: Configure builder.Services.Configure<ApiBehaviorOptions>(o => o.InvalidModelStateResponseFactory = ctx => ...) to build the same ApiErrorResponse envelope GlobalExceptionHandler produces for a thrown ValidationException, sourcing error.details from ModelState.

findings.title: No client-side type models the backend's standard error contract, enabling systemic silent swallowing
findings.description: No ApiError class/interface exists anywhere in the Angular app corresponding to the backend's documented {error:{code,message,details,traceId,timestamp,instance}} envelope. ApiService.handleError() unwraps every HttpErrorResponse into a bare Error object with an unsafely-cast .status property bolted on, discarding error.code, error.details, and error.traceId outright. Because there is no shared, typed error surface for call sites to branch on, roughly two dozen .subscribe({error: () => {}}) blocks and DataPreloadService's uniform catchError(() => of([])) pattern (11 datasets) each independently improvise or skip error handling. This is the root CONTRACT gap; the angular-domain finding describes its component-level symptom.
findings.suggested_fix: Introduce one typed ApiError class built centrally in ApiService.handleError() (code, message, details, traceId, category derived from HTTP status), make it the only error type ApiService ever throws, and require callers to branch on .category instead of improvising per call site.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Confirmed; the contract-level root cause of angular.no-typed-error-contract-silent-swallowing. Note "discards error.details outright" is overstated — handleError does read details[].message; it discards code, traceId (now fixed) and the structured array.

findings.title: A handful of controllers return raw strings/anonymous objects instead of throwing through GlobalExceptionHandler
findings.description: UsageDashboardController, CustomersController, BidSheetController, and DiagnosticsController return ad hoc bodies directly instead of throwing ValidationException/BusinessException, unlike 59 call sites across 24 other files that correctly throw typed exceptions. The bare-string case is worst: ASP.NET serializes it as a raw JSON string body, and Angular's handleError() fallback chain cannot extract anything from a plain string, so it falls through to a generic error message instead of the intended user-facing text.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace these with throw new ValidationException(...) / throw new BusinessException(...) so they flow through GlobalExceptionHandler like the rest of the app.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615.

findings.title: The only real producer of HTTP 429 never gets a Retry-After header or the standard envelope
findings.description: Program.cs's AddRateLimiter fixed-window limiter is the sole path in the codebase that returns 429. No OnRejected callback is configured, so the rejection is written directly by RateLimiterMiddleware with an empty body and no headers, entirely bypassing GlobalExceptionHandler. GlobalExceptionHandler's own code that sets Retry-After: 30 for statusCode 429 is therefore dead code for the one status it explicitly names, since exceptions never produce 429 in this app.
findings.suggested_fix: Configure options.OnRejected on AddRateLimiter to write the standard ApiErrorResponse envelope and set Retry-After before returning.

findings.title: Diagnostics elevator-geocoding bypasses the app's own nominatim retry/circuit-breaker pipeline
findings.description: GeocodeService correctly resolves nominatim calls via httpFactory.CreateClient("nominatim"), which Program.cs wires with a 10s timeout, 3-attempt exponential-backoff-with-jitter retry, and a circuit breaker. DiagnosticsController.PopulateElevatorCache and GeocodeElevatorsBackground instead call the bare unconfigured default client directly against the same host, with no timeout/retry/circuit-breaker, only a per-item catch(Exception) that logs a warning and continues. A nominatim outage burns through the entire elevator list with zero circuit protection.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the client via httpFactory.CreateClient("nominatim") in both diagnostics geocoding paths instead of the default client.

findings.title: Catalog/lookup endpoints swallow backend dependency failures into HTTP 200 with empty or partial data
findings.description: EntitlementsController.GetCatalog and NotesController.GetMentionCatalog wrap their DB lookups in catch(Exception), log at Warning, and return Ok(...) with an empty or partially-populated response regardless -- the HTTP status never reflects the failure. This is the server-side mirror of the Angular client's inability to distinguish genuinely-empty from failed: for these two endpoints, the ambiguity originates in the API itself.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a degraded (or per-section) flag to these responses instead of silently returning indistinguishable-from-success empty/partial data.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Confirmed and deliberate today (the log text says "returning empty lists"). Whether the mention picker should 503 instead of degrading is a product call.

findings.title: Backend traceId is generated and returned but the Angular client never reads or surfaces it
findings.description: CorrelationIdMiddleware generates/propagates a traceId into every error response body and the X-Correlation-Id response header. api.service.ts's handleError() extracts message/details from the error body but never reads error.error.error.traceId, and no UI surface ever displays it. An Unexpected/Infrastructure error's traceId should be shown to the user so they can share it with support; currently no error surfaced by this app gives the user any reference id.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract traceId in handleError() (fold into the typed ApiError), and have error toasts append (Ref: {traceId}) for Infrastructure/Unexpected categories.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615.

findings.title: Client error handling branches on 403 but has no equivalent branch for 401
findings.description: api.service.ts's handleError() special-cases status===403 with a toast, but has no branch for 401 -- an authentication failure from the API (session expired/revoked) falls through to the generic error path. Combined with the widespread swallowing pattern, this typically means the user sees nothing instead of a session-expired message.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 401 branch to handleError() that triggers re-authentication (msalService.loginRedirect()) or a session-expired toast, mirroring the existing 403 branch.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615.

findings.title: Client-side retry on transient failures is applied ad hoc in only 2 of dozens of call sites
findings.description: Only bid-sheet.component.ts and build-list.component.ts apply any retry/timeout handling. The other ~90+ ApiService call sites either have no timeout at all or catchError straight to a fallback with zero retry, so a single transient network blip is indistinguishable from a permanent failure everywhere else in the app.
findings.suggested_fix: Move a standard retry({count,delay}) into ApiService's shared pipeline for idempotent GETs rather than leaving it to individual components to opt in ad hoc.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] The two call sites with retry are the slow ODS scans where a transient blip is likely and worth retrying; blanket retry would multiply load during an outage. Recorded in STYLE-DEVIATIONS.md.

findings.title: Trade-unit filter fails silently (no log/error) when a decorated action's parameters don't match its 3 recognized shapes
findings.description: EnforceTradeUnitAccessAttribute recognizes exactly 3 parameter shapes (List<string> tradeUnits, string tradeUnitKey, body objects/collections with a TradeUnitKey property). If none match, it runs the entitlements-availability check and then calls next() with zero enforcement and zero logging. Investigated as a suspected cross-trade-unit bypass on StoredGrain/DpContracts specifically: that turned out to be a false alarm at the data-access level, since StoredGrainService.GetAllAsync and DpContractService.GetAllAsync each independently call IUserEntitlementService.GetAllowedTradeUnitCodesAsync and fail closed (503) if entitlements are unavailable, proven by DpContractServiceTests.cs. The silent-noop design defect in the attribute itself is still real and already caused one live gap in the past (H-061, DELETE actualharvest/{id}, fixed 2026-09-09 by moving the check into the service layer) with no test forcing loud failure on a future recurrence.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an else branch that logs a warning whenever none of the 3 patterns match anything in ActionArguments, and add a regression test asserting that log fires for an unrecognized shape.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615.

findings.title: No Role/Permission/RolePermission/UserRole data model or resource:action:scope permissions exist anywhere in the app
findings.description: The style guide requires Roles/Permissions/RolePermissions/UserRoles EF Core entities, resource:action[:scope]-formatted permission strings, an IPermissionService/[RequirePermission] pipeline, and a GET /api/me/permissions endpoint. This app has none of that: authorization is instead a single Azure-AD-issued Admin app role plus a config-driven UsageDashboard:ViewAll allowlist, with all other access control delegated to trade-unit entitlement data-scoping (tenant/data scoping, not RBAC). Functionally this appears correctly enforced end-to-end for the app's actual (nearly binary) authorization needs, but it is a full architectural deviation from the style guide nowhere acknowledged as a deliberate choice the way AR-01 through AR-08 document other deviations.
findings.suggested_fix: Record this as a deliberate architectural deviation (a new SECURITY-REVIEWS or ADR entry) explaining that a full RBAC model was scoped out in favor of a single Admin role plus entitlement-based data scoping.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Deliberate: authorization is two Azure AD app roles plus trade-unit data scoping. Adding a permissions table would mean a second source of truth beside AAD group membership, which is where access is actually administered. Documented in docs/application-context/SECURITY-MODEL.md.

findings.title: No in-app audit trail for role/access-list changes
findings.description: The style guide requires logging role_assigned/role_removed/role_modified/privilege_escalation events. Because Admin membership lives entirely in an Azure AD Super Users group and the UsageDashboard:ViewAll list lives in appsettings config, neither is ever mutated through app code, so none of these events can appear in the app's own telemetry -- that history only exists in Azure AD's own audit log and config/deployment history. SecurityAuditMiddleware does log 401/403 outcomes, the one style-guide event type genuinely covered.
findings.suggested_fix: If in-app visibility into privilege changes is ever needed, have the app periodically snapshot Super-Users-group membership into its own audit log. Low priority given the trusted/internal user population.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Follows from the above: Admin membership lives in an AAD group and the ViewAll list in config, so neither is ever mutated through app code and these events cannot exist in our telemetry. That history is in Azure AD's audit log. Documented in SECURITY-MODEL.md.

findings.title: Five largest Angular feature components (up to 4180 lines) have zero test coverage
findings.description: build-list, bid-sheet, home, dashboard, and customer-list components carry the app's densest business logic (bid pricing, multi-fetch race-guarded data loading, contract/print orchestration) with no .spec.ts at all. build-list.component.ts alone has 446 occurrences of price/calc/margin/freight/sort/filter keywords, confirming dense untested business logic. A regression in filtering, sorting, or pricing display logic inside any of these would only surface via manual QA or a user-reported bug, not CI.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract pure business logic (filtering/sorting/pricing helpers) into testable functions/services first, then add component specs for the highest-traffic user flows.

findings.title: 16 of 21 Infrastructure repositories have zero direct test coverage, including the two largest
findings.description: Measured via direct-instantiation grep across the test project: only 5 of 21 repositories have any direct test evidence. TicketRepository.cs (729 lines) and UsageRepository.cs (915 lines) have no test file exercising them at all, direct or indirect -- a silent regression in ticket status filtering or usage-aggregation SQL would ship undetected since the green 535/535 dotnet test run never touches these classes. CustomerRepository.cs (843 lines) and ContractRepository.cs (444 lines) are also only covered by a single static pure-function helper each.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an in-memory-EF or WebApplicationFactory-backed test class for TicketRepository and UsageRepository first (mirroring the existing DailyRecapGroupRepositoryTests.cs/SavedListRepositoryTests.cs pattern), covering at least one read and one write/aggregate path each.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Confirmed; duplicate of dotnet.repository-test-coverage-gap. Note the count is if anything understated: UsageRepository's two "test mentions" are Mock<IUsageRepository>, which never runs the implementation.

findings.title: UserEntitlementService's SQL-outage fail-open/fail-closed cache logic has only 1 of ~6 behavioral branches tested
findings.description: UserEntitlementServiceTests.cs contains exactly one [Fact], covering only the customer-has-no-trade-unit-mapping deny path. The SqlException handler in GetAllowedTradeUnitCodesAsync -- which serves a 10-minute last-known-good cache on a transient DB outage, or fails closed to an empty set with no cache -- is completely untested, as is ValidateTradeUnitsOrThrowAsync's deny path and the has-access/no-access branches of ValidateCustomerAccessAsync. This is the exact security-critical logic the class's own doc comment calls fail-closed, not silently allow -- a regression here could silently flip to fail-open (serving all trade units) or incorrectly fail-closed (denying all access) during a DB blip, undetected by the green test suite.
findings.suggested_fix: Add tests for: SqlException with a warm cache returns last-known-good; SqlException with no cache fails closed to empty set; ValidateTradeUnitsOrThrowAsync throws on a denied code; ValidateCustomerAccessAsync allows/denies correctly.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615.

The sibling CalendarDateJsonConverter in the same folder has a dedicated test file, but these two do not, so a future edit to the Kind-normalization branches could silently reintroduce either bug with no CI signal.

findings.title: UsageAggregationBackgroundService's day-rollover and interval-gating logic has zero test coverage
findings.description: RunCycleAsync contains date-boundary branching (aggregate-once-per-day with a late-arrival re-run window, Sunday-triggered weekly rollup, and three independently-gated interval checks) plus a catch-all that silently swallows and logs any exception. None of this scheduling/date-math logic is exercised by any test; a day-boundary or day-of-week off-by-one would silently skip or double-run a weekly rollup with no CI signal.

Changing planting year, navigating away, and returning silently re-applies figures from whichever year was last cached.

Rapid year/TU navigation lets an older response land after a newer one, overwriting current estimates/market-share/harvest figures with stale data.

findings.title: Saved-list NLQ result cache (customerIds) is never invalidated as the customer roster grows
findings.description: The cache is reset only on trade-unit change or switching saved lists, not when customers() itself grows via progressive per-producer merges (a pattern the file's own comments document). Newly-arrived customers that would match a saved list's query stay silently excluded from results until the user reselects the list or changes trade units.
findings.suggested_fix: Invalidate the customerIds cache whenever customers() materially changes, not only on TU/list change.

findings.title: Selecting a linked producer never cancels in-flight per-customer fetches, unlike every other selection path
findings.description: handleSelectCustomer and _onTradeUnitsChanged both call this._cancelSelection$.next() before firing per-customer fetches, all piped through takeUntil(this._cancelSelection$). handleSelectLinkedCustomer skips this call. Clicking linked producer B then C quickly leaves B's in-flight fetch uncancelled; if it resolves after C is selected, data fields get silently overwritten with B's stale data while C is displayed.
findings.suggested_fix: Call this._cancelSelection$.next() at the top of handleSelectLinkedCustomer, matching the other selection paths.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615. [2026-09-21 re-verified] Confirmed in code: handleSelectLinkedCustomer now calls this._cancelSelection$.next() at the top, matching handleSelectCustomer.

findings.title: Planting-intentions cache-hit path never bumps the in-flight request counter, unlike the cache-miss path
findings.description: The cache-miss branch increments _piRequestId before fetching so an older in-flight request becomes stale by comparison; the cache-hit branch sets signals directly without bumping the counter. An older, uncancellable in-flight fetch can still land and overwrite the freshly-restored cached data because its captured request id still matches.
findings.suggested_fix: Increment _piRequestId on every selection path, including the cache-hit branch.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615. [2026-09-21 re-verified] Confirmed in code: the cache-hit branch now does `++this._piRequestId` before setting signals.

findings.title: DP-contracts fetch in build-list can reapply stale-trade-unit data after the shared cache was correctly reset
findings.description: DataPreloadService calls appState.clearDpContractsCache() reactively on trade-unit change. BuildListComponent._ensureDpForQuery() has no request-id or TU-match check on its response handler, only a guard against a second concurrent call. If the user switches trade units while a DP fetch for the old TU is in flight, the reset fires first, then the stale response lands and calls appState.setDpContracts(data), re-flipping dpContractsLoaded=true with the wrong trade unit's rows, silently corrupting a cache shared across the whole app.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture the trade-unit key at fetch start and discard the response in _ensureDpForQuery's subscribe if appState.selectedTradeUnits() no longer matches it.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615. [2026-09-21 re-verified] Confirmed in code: _ensureDpForQuery now captures fetchedForTu and checks an isStale() closure before writing the response into the shared cache.

findings.title: Ticket self-heal effect can adopt another trade unit's ticket data
findings.description: _appStateTicketsEffect compares appState.tickets().length > this.tickets().length with no check that the appState data actually belongs to the currently selected trade unit. appState.tickets is cleared by a separate singleton (DataPreloadService, via clearTicketsCache()) reacting independently to the same selectedTradeUnits signal this component's own _tuEffect/_loadFresh(true) reacts to. Angular gives no ordering guarantee between these two independent subscribers, so during a trade-unit switch there's a window where this component's local tickets is already [] (freshly cleared for the new TU) while appState.tickets still holds the previous TU's larger set -- the effect then copies the old TU's tickets into the new TU's context and marks _ticketsReady=true, letting a ticket-dependent query silently run against the wrong trade unit's deliveries.
findings.suggested_fix: Tag cached ticket data with the trade-unit key it was fetched for (or re-check appState.selectedTradeUnits() matches) before adopting it, instead of a bare length comparison.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615. [2026-09-21 re-verified] Confirmed in code: _appStateTicketsEffect now compares appState.ticketsTradeUnitKey() against the currently selected TU and bails before adopting on a mismatch, with a comment naming this exact race.

findings.title: Free-text unconfirmed-contract NLQ query uses narrower logic than the canonical rule used everywhere else

The canonical isContractUnconfirmed(), documented as the same rule the Insights Unconfirmed Contracts category and this same file's refine-panel checkbox use, treats NULL/empty status as unconfirmed too. A contract that's never had a confirmation status set (the most common unconfirmed case) appears in Insights and the refine-panel checkbox but is silently dropped from producers-with-unconfirmed-contracts typed into Build A List.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the inline check in applyContractFilters with a call to the shared isContractUnconfirmed(ct) helper.

findings.title: New bid-sheet location inserts aren't protected against the same unique-constraint race the rest of the class handles
findings.description: BidSheetRepository.BulkUpsertBidsAsync saves newly-discovered BidSheetLocation rows via a bare SaveChangesAsync with no try/catch, while CreateLocationAsync and UpdateLocationAsync both wrap their saves in a catch for unique violations and attempt reconciliation. If two concurrent bid-sheet submissions both need to create the same new location (same Name+TradeUnitCode, unique index), one throws an unhandled DbUpdateException and the entire bulk save fails (whole batch of bids lost) instead of reconciling like every other collision path in the file.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the new-location SaveChangesAsync call in the same IsUniqueViolation catch/reconcile pattern used elsewhere in the class.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615. Same root cause as the already-logged SecurityAuditMiddleware finding: pipeline position assumes a normal return that the framework short-circuits on exceptions, undercounting real error-rate/session data specifically for the failures that matter most.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the downstream call in try/finally so the activity record (with the real or a synthesized 5xx status code) is always recorded regardless of exception.

The same query+limit returns a different-shaped result depending purely on cache warmth -- a disambiguation dropdown that showed 5 candidates on first search silently shows 1 on the next identical search.

findings.title: GeocodeBatchAsync doesn't use the shared rate-limiting semaphore, allowing bursts past Nominatim's 1 req/sec policy
findings.description: GeocodeService is registered as a singleton specifically so _rateLimiter (SemaphoreSlim) and _lastNominatimCall serialize all Nominatim calls across concurrent requests; GeocodeSingleAsync and SearchAsync both acquire the semaphore first. GeocodeBatchAsync never touches either, only self-pacing with its own internal 1100ms delay between items in its own loop. Two concurrent callers will send simultaneous requests to Nominatim, violating the documented 1 req/sec limit and risking an IP-level throttle that would break geocoding app-wide.
findings.suggested_fix: Have GeocodeBatchAsync acquire _rateLimiter and honor _lastNominatimCall the same way GeocodeSingleAsync does.

findings.title: In-flight HTTP request dedup cache can be evicted while the underlying call is still pending
findings.description: ApiService._dedupe() builds request.pipe(shareReplay({bufferSize:1, refCount:false}), finalize(() => this._inFlight.delete(key))). Because finalize sits downstream of shareReplay, its teardown runs per individual subscriber's own unsubscribe, not once when the shared underlying HTTP call itself completes. DataPreloadService subscribes to these calls inside a switchMap keyed on trade-unit selection; switching trade units unsubscribes from the old TU's in-flight request, which immediately deletes its _inFlight cache entry even though refCount:false keeps the real HTTP call alive in the background. Switching back to that TU before the original response lands fires a brand-new duplicate HTTP request against the same endpoint the cache exists to protect.
findings.suggested_fix: Move finalize upstream of shareReplay (request.pipe(finalize(...), shareReplay(...))) so cleanup ties to the shared source's completion, not each subscriber's teardown.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] Fixed on branch fix_AuditPhase1Findings, merged to main 2026-09-21 via PR #615. [2026-09-21 re-verified] Confirmed in code: _dedupe() now pipes finalize(...) upstream of shareReplay(...), with a comment explaining exactly why the ordering matters for switchMap-driven unsubscription.

findings.title: A refine change can be permanently stranded if it lands while a different note-scope fetch is in flight
findings.description: _ensureNotesForQuery is a no-op whenever _scopedNotesFetchInFlight is already true, silently dropping the request for the new scope. _commitRefinements calls it exactly once when staging a refine; if that call is swallowed because an older scoped fetch (different keyword/pinned/author/window combo) is still in flight, the older fetch's next handler stores the old scope's key, _criteriaReadiness for the newly staged refine never becomes true, and nothing else re-invokes _ensureNotesForQuery for the new scope. The staged refine (and its loading spinner/disabled Apply) can be stuck until the user makes another refine change.
findings.suggested_fix: When a scoped-notes fetch resolves, re-check the current desired scope (not just the one captured at fetch start) and re-fire _ensureNotesForQuery if it has since changed.

findings.title: Ticket dates compared with local-time getters can misclassify Jan 1 tickets
findings.description: Ticket.date is a bare yyyy-MM-dd string, which the JS Date constructor parses as UTC midnight. hasDeliveriesThisYear then reads d.getFullYear(), a local-time getter, so for any user in a negative-UTC-offset zone (all US time zones), a ticket dated Jan 1 renders as Dec 31 of the prior year, wrongly excluding that delivery from has-deliveries-this-year. The file already has a purpose-built UTC-safe parser (parseNoteTime) for exactly this class of bug on notes, but ticket dates aren't run through an equivalent helper.
findings.suggested_fix: Parse t.date with UTC-aware getters (getUTCFullYear()) or split the yyyy-MM-dd string directly instead of running it through local-time Date getters.

findings.title: 17 subscribe() error handlers in home.component.ts are no-ops, silently swallowing API failures
findings.description: home.component.ts contains 17 occurrences of `error: () => {}` on subscriptions loading stored grain, DP contracts, planting intentions, notes, last-contacts, and cross-trade-unit customer data. When any of these calls fail, the user sees stale or empty data with no toast, no console/log entry, and no visible error state — and there is no telemetry trail for support to diagnose a report of 'my data is missing'. This is the app's single largest concentration of the same anti-pattern (34 occurrences of the same empty-handler shape exist across 9 files app-wide).
findings.suggested_fix: At minimum log the error (e.g. via the existing GlobalErrorHandler/logging service) even where no user-facing toast is appropriate for a background refresh; consider a subtle inline indicator for stale data when a background load fails.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] New — found during the angular-domain audit pass. Scoped to home.component.ts as the worst offender; the same shape recurs more sparingly elsewhere (e.g. bid-sheet.component.ts) and may be worth a follow-up sweep.
findings.resolution_notes: All 17 empty handlers now call a private _reportBackgroundFailure(what, err): console.error in dev builds, plus one toast per data source per 30s (and at most one toast per 5s overall, so an outage that fails many calls at once produces a single message). No behaviour change on success paths.

findings.title: Unnecessary `as any` casts in bid-sheet.component.ts bypass type checking on an API payload
findings.description: saveLocationName() and toggleLocationScoularStatus() both build an update payload ending in `bids: []` and cast the whole object `as any` before calling apiService.updateBidSheetLocation(id, location: Partial<BidSheetLocation>). BidSheetLocation has no `bids` property, so without the cast TypeScript's excess-property check would flag it — the `as any` exists specifically to hide that mismatch rather than because `any` is genuinely needed, violating the guide's 'Avoid any' rule.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the stray `bids: []` field (Partial<BidSheetLocation> doesn't need it) and remove the `as any` casts, or add `bids` to the model if the API genuinely expects it.
findings.notes: [2026-09-21] New — found during the angular-domain audit pass.
findings.resolution_notes: Dropped the stray bids: [] from both payloads and removed both as-any casts; the objects now type-check as Partial<BidSheetLocation>. Safe server-side: CreateBidSheetLocationRequest.Bids defaults to an empty list and UpdateLocationAsync never reads it.

findings.title: Schema verification script tracks 19 of 99 migrations and 29 of 40 tables
findings.description: scripts/_VerifySchema.sql hand-maintains expected-schema snapshots (@Tables, @Columns, @UniqueIndexes, @Migrations) that are meant to be updated after every migration, per its own header comment. The last update was migration 20260609161126_AddPrintLayoutToBidSheetPreference; the repo now has 99 migration files running through 20260921152258_AddUsageDashboardViewAllUsers, and the live ApplicationDbContextModelSnapshot.cs defines 40 tables and 57 indexes versus the script's 29 tables and 15 unique indexes. Because every one of the ~80 untracked-but-applied migrations and ~11 untracked tables now shows up as a Migration.Extra/Table.Extra WARN row, the script can never again print its single "Database is current" success message -- every run returns a large, permanently-noisy findings list, so a real drift signal (a genuine FAIL row) is buried in expected WARN noise instead of standing out.
findings.suggested_fix: Regenerate the four @Tables/@Columns/@CheckConstraints/@UniqueIndexes/@Migrations sections from the current ApplicationDbContextModelSnapshot.cs, and consider generating this script from the snapshot automatically (or checking it in CI) so it cannot silently drift again.

[2026-09-21] New finding. Confirmed by diffing script counts (19 migrations / 29 tables / 15 unique indexes) against ApplicationDbContextModelSnapshot.cs (99 migration files on disk / 40 tables / 57 indexes).

The regeneration is only the data sections; if it is ever regenerated again, keep the comparison logic untouched and diff the pre-existing rows to prove nothing silently changed. Note the migration count is 49, not 48: 20260513185441_DropCustomerSnapshot.cs is a real migration whose filename contains "Snapshot", so a naive filename filter drops it.

The comparison and reporting logic below those sections is byte-identical to before. Verified by re-parsing both the script and the snapshot independently: the (table, column) sets match in both directions with zero gaps, all 277 pre-existing rows are unchanged, and the 21 index names and 49 migration ids match the repo exactly. Not executed against a live database - sqlcmd is not installed on this machine - so the first real run should be treated as the confirmation step. Also corrected the header, which pointed at the old GrainOriginatorPortal.Api path for the snapshot.

findings.title: GeocodeService.SearchAsync handed back the cached list itself after a cache miss, letting one caller empty the shared entry
findings.description: On a cache hit SearchAsync returned a defensive copy, but on a cache miss it stored the freshly built list in IMemoryCache and returned that same instance. Any caller that mutated its own result mutated the cache entry: clearing the returned list emptied the cached entry, so the next identical search returned zero results until the entry expired. The in-code comment on the cache-hit path already stated the intent ("handing back the cached instance would let any caller mutation corrupt the entry for everyone"); the miss path simply did not follow it.
findings.suggested_fix: Return a copy on the cache-miss path too.
findings.resolution_notes: Fixed by returning a copy on the miss path. Found by a new test written for dotnet.service-layer-test-coverage-gap, which failed against the old code and passes against the fix.

findings.title: The shared dialog cannot be dismissed with the Escape key
findings.description: DialogComponent closes on the X button and on a backdrop click, but registers no keydown handling, so Escape does nothing. Escape-to-dismiss is the expected behaviour for a modal and its absence is an accessibility and keyboard-navigation gap across every consumer of the shared dialog.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a host keydown.escape listener that emits close, gated on the same closeOnBackdrop-style input if opt-out is wanted.
findings.notes: [2026-09-22] Surfaced while writing the dialog spec. Not fixed in that pass because it is a source change and the spec work was scoped to tests only.

findings.title: The dialog close button and the toast dismiss buttons have no accessible name
findings.description: Both are icon-only buttons with no aria-label and no visually hidden text, so a screen reader announces them as an unlabelled button. The new specs have to locate them by position rather than by role and name, which is itself the symptom.
findings.suggested_fix: Add aria-label ("Close dialog", "Dismiss notification") and then tighten the specs to query by accessible name.
